title: Dispatch jobs from a stable ref so merges don't disturb running jobs
summary: Retry of job 20261018-095726-r3bn for the maintainer running Athena: stop rewriting the local branch after a squash merge (the resync_onto_merge call in Athena::land_pr in gh.rs), so the next job can start while the earlier PR is in CI, and one merge still lands one job as one commit. gh.rs is now a deliverable, and the test seam is a crate-private inner function of Athena::land_pr that takes a Remote and host.

defaults_applied.how: All changes are Rust code and tests.
cargo test, clippy and fmt --check are required criteria.
Criteria check merge behavior through tests, not that wiring exists.
Design docs and decisions.md record the rule and rejected alternatives.
One focused change to the post-merge path; the planner-stage change is excluded.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
Removes the resync call rather than working around it at dispatch.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The typed request is a retry of the original dispatch-stability job; the proposed planning-stage change (seam-naming critic, hand-on at the round cap) is a separate job and is not done here.
Goal: the next job starts while the previous PR is in CI. Audience: the maintainer running Athena.
The fault is the resync_onto_merge call after a squash merge in Athena::land_pr (gh.rs, about line 1630). Removing it keeps running jobs' bases as ancestors of HEAD, so land.rs plan still lands them.

A squash conflict against a moved remote tip is handled by cutting the PR head onto the remote tip with Git::replay, which skips commits that become empty. A PrLink source field stops reruns from pushing again, and the fingerprint check before any push stays.

Test seam: Athena::land_pr becomes a thin wrapper over a crate-private inner function taking &dyn Remote and a host. Tests call the inner function with a FakeRemote and a local bare repo. The inner function keeps the former resync call site, so a test fails if the call is restored.

Records commits may sit between landed commits on the local branch. Tests assert no merge commits, A's changes not applied twice, a matching tree fingerprint, and one commit per squash merge, not that B's head holds only B's own commits.
Whether run.rs, pr.rs and watcher.rs change depends on where the dispatch base is read. They are listed with lower probability.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test calls the inner land_pr function with a FakeRemote and host. It squash-merges job A's PR while job B is already dispatched, then checks that B's base commit and worktree are unchanged and B's candidate lands cleanly. Run cargo test.

A test dispatches two jobs back to back before the first merges. After each squash merge, main gains exactly one commit per job, with no merge commits and no rebuild commits. A's changes are not applied twice, and the tree fingerprint matches. Run cargo test.
The test of the second behavior fails if the resync_onto_merge call is restored in the land path. The verifier can check this by reading the test and running cargo test.
cargo test passes, cargo clippy is clean, and cargo fmt --check passes.
No production path calls resync_onto_merge after a merge, and dispatch no longer depends on it having run. Nothing under crates/ refers to it except possibly a removed or renamed definition.

docs/design/parallel-jobs.md, docs/design/native-pr-landing.md and docs/decisions.md state the new base rule, the alternatives rejected, and how a job stale against a moved base is handled by cutting onto the remote tip. A maintainer can read that the next job starts while the earlier PR is in CI and that one merge lands one job.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the change.

out_of_scope: Changing the planning stage, the critic, or the three-round cap (the earlier introspection's proposal is a separate job).
Changes to CI workflows or governance files.
Redesigning the Pages or checks handling in landing.
departures: The change touches the landing path in gh.rs, where the earlier attempt failed in planning. It needs a new seam and several docs, so cost and time sit above the reference and the pass rate below it.
